text:
Maya: Heads-up — this morning eu-west GPU pools hit sustained saturation and queues backed up. I started a quick experiment with soft-priority weights + small preemption window. Want opinions before we flip this to prod.
Sam: Saw the alert. Which routes were most impacted and what's the backlog size?
Maya: Backlog ~1.2k inflight-waiting, median wait went from ~1.8s to ~6.4s for low-priority routes. Mostly /generation and /chat-default. Dedicated customers unchanged. Logs show head-of-line blocking when a few routes submit large batches that fill device slots.
Chen: Is this similar to last month's preemptible-run pattern? Feels like greedy continuous-batching + a couple of large routes.
Oliver: Quick thought: per-route admission + per-pool soft-priority beats pure FIFO at pool level. FIFO leads to noisy neighbor where a high-batch route starves many small low-latency requests. Token-bucket per-route with a global pool signal seems best balance.
Indra: Two implementation concerns: 1) per-route queues increase metrics cardinality and memory; 2) how do we derive a reliable capacity signal? GPU util is noisy (NVLink/CPU stalls).
Kevin: Simpler alternative: keep pool-level FIFO, but add soft-weighting + aging. priority_score = base_priority + age * alpha. Preempt only when priority_score gap > threshold. Also enforce max_batch_duration to prevent huge batches from hogging a slot.
Maya: I prototyped admission change in staging: route token-buckets whose refill rate ties to pool_target_inflight = floor(gpu_slots * concurrency_per_device * safety_margin). Also adding an X-Backpressure header we can return to clients: `X-Backpressure: level=high|med|low, advise=wait|retry-after`. Example config I tested:
```
admission:
  soft_alpha: 0.01
  aging_threshold_s: 30
  preempt_limit_pct: 5
  max_batch_duration_ms: 250
```
Sam: Backpressure headers -> yes please. SDKs can use that to jitter retries and reduce stampeding herd. Can we standardize advise=retry-after for short windows?
Oliver: One edge-case: preemption mid-chat session will flush KV cache. Preempting a chat request can increase tokens on subsequent calls because cache cold-starts. Need affinity rules: keep chat pinned or do soft-throttle for chat routes.
Chen: Agreed. Suggestion: allow preemption only for stateless/ephemeral routes (embedding, rerank, batch generation). For chat, prefer drop-new or slow-path (deprioritize batch size). Also consider spilling KV cache to CPU memory when preempting as fallback.
Indra: We should instrument these metrics before wide rollout: per-route queue length, 95th wait time, preemptions/sec, batch_size histogram, head_of_line_time. Alert: queue_length > 500 for 5m -> page oncall.
Kevin: Cost tradeoff note: per-route isolation will fragment pools and increase infra footprint. Rough estimate: worst-case +8% GPU cost due to fragmentation vs ~30% SLO improvement for low-latency customers. We should gate per-route isolation to Dedicated or high-tier.
Maya: Customer perspective: enterprise customers prioritize predictability and SLOs over marginal cost. We can make per-route isolation an opt-in feature behind Dedicated or a premium flag.
Oliver: Draft runbook (operational):
1) If pool saturates: check avg_batch_size and avg_batch_duration.
2) If avg_batch_size > threshold -> reduce batch_max for offending routes.
3) Enable soft-priority weighting and aging.
4) If sustained >30m, trigger pool autoscale / spin additional pool.
5) Notify affected customers and route-specific SDKs with X-Backpressure.
Sam: I'll run 24h replay on staging with real traces to compare FIFO vs token-bucket per-route vs soft-weighting. Can we define replay configs?
Maya: Please run replay with these params: soft_alpha=0.01, aging_threshold_s=30, preempt_limit_pct=5, max_batch_duration_ms=250. Also test a variant with per-route token-bucket where refill = pool_target_inflight * route_share. I'll attach protos in PR.
deploy-bot: Playback job started by Sam at 2026-03-18 09:12. Job id: replay-9042.
Oliver: :thumbsup: let's not do a hotfix in prod during US peak hours. Schedule rollout in a low-traffic window and enable gradual ramp + canary.
Maya: I'll open a PR with the staging config, a small dashboard for backpressure metrics, and a short runbook. Thanks all for quick feedback.
